questions: Can native OpenClaw write and execute a previously unavailable experiment in a Linux sandbox?
Are every provider request, response, failed slice and workspace version retained before subsequent admission?
Do package execution, reviews, costs and deadlines remain subject to existing gates?

configuration.transport: synthetic Responses API for local regressions; no subscription call

replication_units: Independent deterministic test scenarios; Docker smoke is one development execution, not a research replication.
sample_size_rationale: Enumerated admission, protocol, failure and resume branches; no population inference or confidence intervals.
release_blockers: A provider request can bypass durable admission
A generated command can reach host execution or host credentials
Archive traversal, symlinks or oversized files are accepted
A package can bypass fresh method reviews or original paper limits
Unknown provider outcomes are silently replayed
Required local backend, database, infrastructure or UI checks fail
cases: Same request replay and in-flight refusal
Missing dependency, invalid manifest and failed pilot retained
Exact dependency and source hash verification
Public queue builder progress with no credentials
criteria: All declared local blocking scenarios must pass. AI answer quality and scientific validity require a separately frozen live evaluation before publishing the builder prompt or enabling production.
controls: Separate generated-package runner; arbitrary custom-package switch stays disabled
Synthetic provider has no credentials or network calls
exclusions: Unavailable production credentials, AWS equipment and provider usage are conditional checks and must be reported as unverified, never passed.
stopping: No live provider or AWS calls in this campaign; one bounded Linux smoke per implementation revision unless a failure requires correction. Preserve all failed reports.

reviewers.independence: Implementation author; development inspection only, not independent or human review

coverage_limits: Does not demonstrate arbitrary-paper reproducibility, guarantee conclusive claims, validate causal inference or replace source review. Existing fictitious paper is an exposed regression, not a held-out check.
